children: China has capped increases in retail prices for transportation fuels for the third time since the Iran war began to mitigate the impact of rising international oil prices on the domestic market, the state planner said in a statement on Friday.

Retail prices for gasoline and diesel will rise by 260 yuan ($38.76) and 250 yuan per metric ton, respectively, effective September 12. Under China’s scheduled pricing mechanism, the increases would have been 435 yuan and 420 yuan, respectively, the statement said.
After the adjustment, gasoline and diesel retail prices will be 19% and 21% higher, respectively, than the levels set in the last adjustment before the Iran war began.
